Long ago, Yasin's father was a fisherman in a village by the sea. He went out in his boat every morning at dawn and came back before sunset.

Every evening Yasin waited for him on a rock by the shore.

One day Yasin's father went out — and did not come back.

Then, days later, the news came: sea bandits had taken him captive along with some other fishermen, and they were demanding a lot of money to set them free.

Yasin cried and said to Sheikh Bashir, the imam of the masjid, "Where can we ever get all that money?"

The Sheikh said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Free the captive.' This is a right that a Muslim has over all the Muslims — not only over his own family."

After Jumu'ah prayer, the Sheikh stood up and spoke to the people about the captives. He said, "These are your brothers, and they are waiting for you."

Then he put a wooden box by the door of the masjid.

People came with whatever they had: one with some coins, another with his ring, another with a goat he had sold at the market.

A poor fisherman who owned nothing but his net came and said, "I'll sell it, and make myself another."

Yasin went to his little box where he had been saving his coins for years, to buy a fishing knife like his father's.

He looked at the coins for a long time. Then he carried all of them to the masjid.

When Sheikh Bashir saw him putting his coins in the box, he said, "Yasin, this is your money."

Yasin said, "And that is my father — and his brothers who are with him."

The people of the village collected all the money in one month, and sent it with trustworthy men to where the captives were held.

And every evening Yasin stood on his rock, looking out at the sea.

One evening a white sail appeared far away. As it came closer, Yasin saw his father standing at the front of the ship, waving to him.

Yasin ran along the shore until his clothes were soaking wet.

When the captives came ashore, Yasin's father hugged his son for a long time. Then he walked to the masjid and thanked the people of the village one by one.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Free the captive, feed the hungry, and visit the sick."

📖 Narrated by Al-Bukhari. This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
